input.reply:
Thanks for the request. `toContain` checks array items by strict identity (like `Array.prototype.includes`), so it doesn't accept asymmetric matchers. That's why your example fails.

You can do this today with `toContainEqual`, which uses deep equality and supports asymmetric matchers:

```ts
expect(options).toContainEqual(expect.objectContaining({ label: "apple.ts" }));
```

Extending `toContain` to accept asymmetric matchers would change its documented semantics, so the team would need to decide on that. Jest behaves the same way.

I couldn't run an issue search or check the source in this triage pass. I haven't confirmed whether an earlier issue already covers this, so please check for one before this goes further.
